summary: AI recommendation & auto‑population of Sessions into Attendee agendas

ai.s: Surfaces AI-recommended sessions and exhibitor events for empty slots when attendees open their schedule, added only when the attendee accepts them.
ai.pr: Attendees had to search the programme manually to fill empty schedule slots, with no personalised suggestions.
ai.wy: Core of AI Agenda Builder Phase 1: personalised agendas with explicit consent.
ai.oc: Specified: a suggestion panel with pre-checked sessions for empty slots, excluding overlaps, duplicates, paid sessions and rejected items, within the event limit.

summary: Schedule UX for AI‑populated Sessions (visibility, filtering, removal)

ai.s: Marks AI-recommended sessions in the attendee schedule with a badge and adds a filter and removal that stops the session being recommended again.
ai.pr: Without clear marking, attendees could not tell which schedule items came from AI recommendations or control them.
ai.wy: AI Agenda Builder Phase 1: transparency and user control over AI-generated agenda items.
ai.oc: Specified: an 'AI recommended' badge, a show/hide filter and removal feeding the do-not-recommend list, consistent across web and mobile.

summary: Adding notification setting to mobile app

ai.s: Adds a Notification Settings screen to the mobile app that syncs both ways with the web preferences.
ai.pr: Users could set notification preferences on web but had no equivalent on mobile, forcing a platform switch.
ai.wy: Part of closing the feature gap between web and mobile.
ai.oc: Specified: mobile notification categories and toggles matching web, with changes reflected immediately on both platforms.

summary: Notifications and email flows for AI‑populated Sessions

ai.s: Sends attendees one in-platform notification and, where enabled, one email confirming the AI-recommended sessions they accepted.
ai.pr: Attendees accepting AI recommendations would have no record of what was added to their schedule.
ai.wy: AI Agenda Builder Phase 1: confirmation-style notifications consistent with the consent model.
ai.oc: Specified: a batched notification per acceptance linking to the schedule, a single summary email, and nothing sent when all recommendations are dismissed.

summary: Adding reset password setting to mobile app

ai.s: Adds a Change Password option to mobile app settings so users can update their password without switching to the web.
ai.pr: The mobile app had no way to change the account password, so users had to switch to the web platform.
ai.wy: Closing the settings gap between mobile and web.
ai.oc: Specified: authenticated users verify their current password and set a new one in-app, mirroring the web flow.

summary: Ongoing AI agenda maintenance & repopulation

ai.s: Recomputes AI session recommendations fresh each time an attendee opens their schedule, reflecting new sessions and changed free slots.
ai.pr: Recommendations need to stay current as the programme and the attendee's schedule change.
ai.wy: AI Agenda Builder Phase 1 uses on-demand computation rather than scheduled batch rebuilds.
ai.oc: Specified: each trigger generates a new set from the current programme, schedule, categories and reject list, never re-showing rejected or accepted sessions.

summary: Bridging UI gap between web and mobile on ExpoFP

ai.s: Aligns the ExpoFP stand content card order on mobile with web, showing Exhibitor Information before Sessions.
ai.pr: On mobile the stand card rendered Sessions, Exhibitor Information, Sessions, breaking the visual hierarchy used on web.
ai.wy: Consistency between the web and mobile ExpoFP experience.
ai.oc: The mobile stand content card is to display Exhibitor Information followed by Sessions.

summary: DS algorithm implementation & calibration for AI Agenda Builder

ai.s: Implements the Data Science recommendation algorithm that ranks sessions for attendees' empty slots by category overlap.
ai.pr: AI Agenda Builder had no algorithm to pick the best-matching sessions for each empty schedule slot.
ai.wy: Enables the Visitor team to surface quality suggestions in the consent UI, reusing existing recommender infrastructure.
ai.oc: Specified: a ranked per-slot list with relevance scores, applying exclusion rules and the event limit, validated against historical event data.

summary: (UI/UX) AI Assistant Chat Entry Point - Web

ai.s: Adds a floating AI assistant chat widget to the event website, with quick actions and free-text questions answered from event data.
ai.pr: Attendees had no visible entry point on the event website to ask the AI assistant questions about the event.
ai.wy: AI Event Assistant: instant answers without navigating between pages; DS owns the backend, web owns the UI.
ai.oc: Specified: a widget visible on page load with a welcome message, at least 3 quick actions, free-text input and graceful out-of-scope handling.

summary: AI Assistant Chat Entry Point - Mobile

ai.s: Adds the AI assistant chat to the mobile app, using the same backend API and quick actions as the web assistant.
ai.pr: Attendees on mobile could not reach the AI assistant without switching to a browser.
ai.wy: AI Event Assistant: on-the-go access for attendees through the shared DS backend.
ai.oc: Specified: an in-app chat interface with welcome message, quick actions and free-text questions, connected to the shared chatbot API.

summary: Speaker Queries

ai.s: Enables the AI event assistant to answer questions about speakers, their bios and the sessions they present.
ai.pr: Attendees wanting speaker information had to browse the programme themselves; the assistant had no speaker knowledge domain.
ai.wy: Speakers are the second core knowledge domain in Phase 1 of the AI Event Assistant.
ai.oc: Specified: a speakers tool for keynote, profile, speaker-to-session and topic queries, stating when no speaker matches instead of fabricating.

summary: P2: Exhibitor and Booth Location Queries

ai.s: Enables the AI event assistant to find exhibitors by category and return booth locations.
ai.pr: Attendees on large exhibition floors had no quick way to find relevant companies or locate a booth.
ai.wy: Phase 2 of the AI Event Assistant adds exhibitors and booths as a knowledge domain.
ai.oc: Specified: an exhibitors tool answering category, startup, booth location and demo/giveaway queries, stating clearly when no exhibitor matches.

summary: P2: Product Showcase Queries

ai.s: Enables the AI event assistant to answer questions about showcased products and which exhibitors offer them.
ai.pr: Attendees with particular product interests had to browse booths individually to find relevant exhibitors.
ai.wy: Phase 2 of the AI Event Assistant adds product showcase data as a knowledge domain.
ai.oc: Specified: a products tool linked to exhibitor records, answering topic, product and exhibitor product queries and stating when nothing matches.

summary: Nearby Hotels & Services Queries (good to have)

ai.s: Optionally lets the AI event assistant answer questions about hotels and services near the venue, if a data source is confirmed.
ai.pr: Travelling attendees could not find nearby accommodation or services within the platform; the data is not held there.
ai.wy: Good-to-have for the AI Event Assistant MVP, only if a data source is confirmed in Phase 2.
ai.oc: Specified: nearby hotel answers from organiser-provided or approved external data, never fabricated; not to be built without a confirmed source.

summary: LLM Model Evaluation & Selection

ai.s: Evaluates and selects the LLM for the AI event assistant MVP on accuracy, latency and cost per query.
ai.pr: The PoC did not optimise which LLM was used, which is not viable for a production MVP.
ai.wy: Accurate, fast answers within a sustainable cost envelope for the production assistant.
ai.oc: Specified: a benchmark suite over session, speaker, exhibitor and product queries, 2 to 3 models compared, a documented choice integrated into the MVP.

summary: Scalability & Response Latency

ai.s: Designs the AI assistant backend to handle concurrent attendees and traffic bursts with defined latency targets and graceful degradation.
ai.pr: The PoC ran under controlled conditions and was not proven to handle event-level concurrent traffic across web and mobile.
ai.wy: Slow responses reduce engagement; the MVP must perform during peak periods such as after keynotes.
ai.oc: Specified: latency targets validated under simulated load, burst handling without errors, and a clear message when the assistant is at capacity.

summary: [Phase 1] Automated post-event CSAT email to visitors about platform experience

ai.s: Sends visitors an automated post-event CSAT email to rate the platform experience in one click, without logging in.
ai.pr: There was no systematic signal from the highest-volume persona on the quality of the platform itself, as opposed to the event.
ai.wy: Product feedback: actionable CSAT on the app, registration, networking and agenda tools.
ai.oc: Specified: a branded email after a configurable delay, 1-5 score plus optional text, tokenised links, GDPR unsubscribe, attributed responses and check-in exclusion toggle.

summary: [Phase 1] Third-party feedback tool evaluation and selection

ai.s: Evaluates at least 3 third-party feedback tools and recommends one to power email-based CSAT/NPS collection.
ai.pr: No tool had been chosen for email CSAT/NPS, blocking Phase 1 build; the choice affects integration effort, cost, GDPR and portability.
ai.wy: A prerequisite decision for the NPS/Feedback Collection programme.
ai.oc: Specified: tools such as Delighted, Survicate and Typeform assessed against set criteria, a signed-off recommendation, effort estimate and GDPR/residency check.

summary: [Phase 1] Automated post-event CSAT email to exhibitors about platform tools

ai.s: Sends exhibitors an automated post-event CSAT email about platform tools such as lead capture, matchmaking and the exhibitor portal.
ai.pr: There was no structured feedback from exhibitors on the tools they use most intensively during events.
ai.wy: Exhibitor CSAT is high-value product signal given their commercial relationship and likely response.
ai.oc: Specified: branded email after a configurable delay, 1-5 score, optional most-useful-tool and open-text questions, tokenised links, primary-contact default.

summary: [Phase 1] Automated post-event NPS email to organizers about Expo Platform

ai.s: Sends organisers a post-event NPS email about ExpoPlatform, with detractor scores alerting Customer Success for follow-up.
ai.pr: There was no systematic B2B NPS from organisers, the strongest leading indicator of renewal intent.
ai.wy: Retention: track client satisfaction and identify at-risk accounts early.
ai.oc: Specified: 0-10 NPS email to the primary organiser contact, optional reason, 30-day frequency cap, CS alert on 0-6 and unsubscribes flagged to CS.
